hypotheses: A topos morphism f:Sh(C)→Sh(D), a sheaf G on D, F=f^-1G.
conclusions: There is a commuting square of the slice topoi and an induced localized morphism f' whose inverse image is the induced application of f^-1 to an arrow over G, satisfying f'_*j_F^-1=j_G^-1f_*.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:C→D from u:D→C, V∈D, U=u(V), F=h_U#=f^-1h_V#, G=h_V#.
conclusions: The topos localization square built from f and F,G agrees with the site-localization square under the slice-site identifications.

hypotheses: A topos morphism f:Sh(C)→Sh(D), sheaves F on C, G on D, and s:F→f^-1G.
conclusions: A base-changed localization square and composition identity exist, with explicitly stated inverse-image formula and a naturality square.
lemma-relocalize-morphism-topoi.hold_reason: The statement declares f':Sh(C)/f^-1 G→Sh(D)/F, but F is a sheaf on C, not D. Source codomain is ill-typed; confirm correction to Sh(D)/G before standalone certification.

hypotheses: A site morphism f:C→D from u:D→C, object V in D, arrow c:U→u(V), and induced map s:h_U#→f^-1h_V#.
conclusions: The relocalized diagram from site morphisms agrees with the slice-topos relocalization diagram under the respective equivalences.
lemma-relocalize-morphism-compare.hold_reason: The statement sets h_U# = f^-1h_V# for arbitrary c:U→u(V), which is generally false unless U=u(V). Source premise needs adjudication before certification.

hypotheses: A site C, functor u:C→Sets, and a representable presheaf h_U.
conclusions: Its stalk at p=u is canonically isomorphic to u(U), functorially in U.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→Sets and its induced precomposition functor u^p:Sets→PSh(C).
conclusions: The functor u^p is right adjoint to the stalk functor PSh(C)→Sets.

hypotheses: A site C, functor u:C→Sets satisfying covering surjectivity and surjectivity on the specified covering-pullback squares.
conclusions: The presheaf u^pE is a sheaf for every set E.
Stalks on sheaves are left adjoint to u^s:Sets→Sh(C).
Every presheaf and its sheafification have the same stalk at u.

hypotheses: A site point p=u:C→Sets, infinite S0 containing every u(U) as subset, and S=P(S0) with site of sets and jointly surjective covering families.
conclusions: Sh(pt) is equivalent to Sh(S).
The functor u:C→S gives a morphism of sites S→C.
Its associated topos morphism composed with the equivalence from Sh(pt) equals (p_*,p^-1).

hypotheses: A point p:Sh(pt)→Sh(C) and a set E.
conclusions: There are canonical maps E→(p_*E)_p→E whose composite is identity.

hypotheses: A point p of a topos of sheaves.
conclusions: p_* preserves limits and coequalizers, is left exact and faithful, preserves surjections, and reflects injections, surjections and isomorphisms.

hypotheses: A site C and functor p=u:C→Sets with cofiltered category of neighbourhoods.
conclusions: The stalk functor defined by the colimit over the opposite neighbourhood category preserves finite limits.

hypotheses: A site C with final object X and fibre products, and u:C→Sets mapping X to a singleton and preserving the specified pullbacks bijectively.
conclusions: The category of neighbourhoods is cofiltered, and the associated stalk functor preserves finite limits.

hypotheses: A site C with finite limits.
conclusions: A point of C is equivalently specified by u:C→Sets preserving finite limits and sending every covering family to a jointly surjective family.

hypotheses: Functors u:C→D, v:D→Sets, and w=v∘u; points/stalks for v and w.
conclusions: The stalk at v of u_pF identifies with the stalk at w of F, naturally in F.

hypotheses: A site morphism f:D→C represented by continuous u:C→D, and a point q on D represented by v:D→Sets.
conclusions: The composite v∘u defines a site point p on C and (f^-1F)_q=F_p for each sheaf F.

hypotheses: A topos morphism f:Sh(D)→Sh(C) and a point q:Sh(pt)→Sh(D).
conclusions: Their composite p=f∘q is a point of Sh(C) and (f^-1F)_q=F_p for every sheaf F.

hypotheses: A site point p=u on C, an object U, and an element x∈u(U).
conclusions: The fibre functor v on C/U taking (V→U) to the preimage of x is a point q, and j_U∘q=p so the stalks of F agree with stalks of its restriction at q.

hypotheses: A point p=u of C, object U, and points of C/U lying over p.
conclusions: The construction q_x for x∈u(U) gives a bijection between these points and u(U).

hypotheses: A site point p=u, object U, and sheaf G on C/U.
conclusions: The stalk of extension by empty set j_{U!}G at p is the coproduct of stalks G_{q_x} over x∈u(U).

hypotheses: Functor u,u':C→Sets with a natural transformation t:u'→u.
conclusions: There is a canonical transformation of stalk functors F_{p'}→F_p compatible with t on representables.

hypotheses: A site C with a conservative family of points.
conclusions: Stalkwise injectivity, surjectivity and equality detect their sheaf-level analogues.
Finite limit and finite colimit diagrams are such if and only if every stalkwise diagram is.

hypotheses: A family of site points (p_i,u_i) on C.
conclusions: It is conservative iff every pair of distinct sections of any sheaf on any U is distinguished by some stalk element represented by (U,x).

hypotheses: A site C, object U, and a family of points p_i; for x∈u_i(U) take the associated localized points q_{i,x}.
conclusions: If the p_i are conservative, so are the localized points; in particular enough points descend to each localization C/U.

hypotheses: A family of objects U_i covering the final sheaf epimorphically; each slice site C/U_i has enough points.
conclusions: The site C has enough points.

hypotheses: A continuous u:C→D of sites and a conservative family of points v_i of D such that each v_i∘u defines a point of C.
conclusions: The functor u defines a morphism of sites D→C.

hypotheses: A site C with finite limits in its category and every cover refinable by a finite covering.
conclusions: The site C has enough points.

hypotheses: A site C and objects U_i with a covering of the final sheaf by their representables and each C/U_i satisfying the finite-covering-refinement and finite-limit hypotheses.
conclusions: The site C has enough points.
lemma-criterion-points.hold_reason: The source condition uses coproducts of representable presheaves h_{U_i} as a map to the final object in Sh(C), without sheafification. A typed comparison needs clarification.

hypotheses: A site C and object U.
conclusions: Every covering of U splits after sheafification at h_U# if and only if every sheaf surjection induces a surjection on sections over U.
